decisions.mark: distinguishes the two ways to substitute an allocator — a COMPILE-time pair of macros versus a RUNTIME pair of function pointers — and states that they are mutually exclusive
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "Option A, compile time. Define both macros in your user config... Option B, runtime. Define only `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY`, then call `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free(my_calloc, my_free)`... The macros take precedence over the runtime setter, and `platform.c` drops its pointer code entirely in that case." | WHY: It distinguishes the compile-time macro pair from the runtime function-pointer pair, and says the macros drop the pointer code entirely, so the two are exclusive in effect. The word "exclusive" never appears, though. || QUOTE: "Option A, compile time. Define both macros in your user config... Option B, runtime. Define only `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY`, then call `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free(my_calloc, my_free)`... The macros take precedence over the runtime setter, and `platform.c` drops its pointer code entirely in that case." | WHY: The answer separates a compile-time macro pair from a runtime function-pointer pair. It also says the macros take precedence and `platform.c` drops its pointer code when they are defined, so the two are alternatives, not combined. || QUOTE: "Both macros must be defined together, or neither. The macros take precedence over the runtime setter, and `platform.c` drops its pointer code entirely in that case." | WHY: The answer separates compile-time macros from runtime function pointers. It says the macros override the runtime setter and remove the pointer code, which makes the two mechanisms mutually exclusive.

decisions.mark: identifies the buffer allocator (MBEDTLS_MEMORY_BUFFER_ALLOC_C) as the only in-tree user of the runtime setter, installing itself over the pointers from its init function
decisions.detail: QUOTE: The library provides its own allocator in `library/memory_buffer_alloc.c`, a first-fit allocator over one caller-supplied buffer. Its init, `mbedtls_memory_buffer_alloc_init()` (line 566), zeroes the static heap, sets the calloc/free pair to its own functions through `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free()` (lines 572 and 575), and writes the first block header. This is the only place the library installs an allocator itself. | WHY: The answer names the buffer allocator's init function as installing itself via the runtime setter and says it is the only place the library does so. || QUOTE: Its init, `mbedtls_memory_buffer_alloc_init()` (line 566), zeroes the static heap, sets the calloc/free pair to its own functions through `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free()` (lines 572 and 575)... This is the only place the library installs an allocator itself. | WHY: The answer names the buffer allocator's init function as installing its own calloc/free via the runtime setter, and says it is the only in-tree place that does so. || QUOTE: "Its init, `mbedtls_memory_buffer_alloc_init()` (line 566), zeroes the static heap, sets the calloc/free pair to its own functions through `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free()` (lines 572 and 575)... This is the only place the library installs an allocator itself." | WHY: The answer names the buffer allocator's init function calling the runtime setter and says it is the only place the library installs an allocator.

decisions.mark: states that the buffer allocator installs a MUTEXED pair when MBEDTLS_THREADING_C is on and a plain pair otherwise, chosen at compile time inside its init function
decisions.detail: QUOTE: The buffer allocator adds a mutex when `MBEDTLS_THREADING_C` is on, and its free path checks block magic values. | WHY: The answer says a mutex is added under MBEDTLS_THREADING_C but never says a mutexed vs plain pair of calloc/free is installed, nor that the choice is made at compile time inside the init function. || QUOTE: The buffer allocator adds a mutex when `MBEDTLS_THREADING_C` is on, and its free path checks block magic values. | WHY: The answer says a mutex is added under MBEDTLS_THREADING_C but never states that init installs a mutexed vs. plain calloc/free pair chosen at compile time. || QUOTE: The buffer allocator adds a mutex when `MBEDTLS_THREADING_C` is on, and its free path checks block magic values. | WHY: The answer says a mutex is added under MBEDTLS_THREADING_C but never states that init chooses between a mutexed and a plain calloc/free pair at compile time.

decisions.mark: states that the buffer allocator itself requires MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY, so enabling it alone is not enough to route the library's allocations through it
